source.title: Forbidden Backrooms: Self-Chat with a Refusal-Abliterated LLM

record.tranche_reason: The post uses a published refusal-abliterated Gemma variant to study self-chat rollouts. It does not measure the refusal direction, apply its ablation, or report a direct test of refusal behavior.
record.gate_note: The post compares self-chat transcripts from vanilla and refusal-abliterated variants, using classifier separability, clustering, and safety screening. These results concern self-chat transcript differences, not the refusal behavior or capability named by the claim versions. The harmful seed prompts explicitly invite harmful behavior, so the resulting behavior is not evidence of behavior without that inducement. The post did not perform the weight edit; it used the linked artifact. The model publisher's capability evidence is cited, not tested here.
record.test_reason: The post uses a published ARA-abliterated Gemma-4 31B artifact to compare self-chat transcripts with the vanilla model. It never measures a refusal direction, applies an ablation, or reports refusal rates or capability. All results concern transcript separability, clustering and safety screening, so no claim version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The author finds the transcripts distinguishable, with harm pressure increasing separability. They are unsure what to conclude and call the jailbroken model's takeover talk under the explicit harm seed unsurprising. The author also flags a confound: differences may come from edit side effects rather than refusal itself.
record.recipe_differences: The post uses an existing ARA-produced refusal-jailbroken artifact and does not measure or apply the original difference-in-means direction method.
record.method_sensitivity: Transcript separability is reported to increase as seed prompts add more harm pressure.

fits_no_version.finding: Self-chat transcripts from vanilla and abliterated Gemma-4 31B are separable under the freedom seed. TF/IDF reached AUC 0.898 and embeddings AUC 0.884.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal abliteration changes a model's open-ended self-chat distribution in detectable ways, even without harmful prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: Separability rises as seed prompts add harm pressure. Vanilla raises safety concerns under freedom_dark; the abliterated model pursues takeover schemes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Behavioural divergence between abliterated and vanilla models grows with harm pressure in the prompt.

fits_no_version.finding: The vanilla model yields purer embedding clusters. Llama Guard flags are concentrated on the freedom_dark seed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Abliterated models show less clustered self-chat content than their parent instruct model.

record.problems: The post does not directly measure refusals or general capability, and uses an existing altered artifact rather than conducting the edit. Harmful behavior is elicited with prompts that explicitly suggest or request it. Trial 2, cluster-purity, and safety-screening outcomes are described without numerical results. Classifier scores measure transcript separability, not the direction or refusal behavior in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No directly relevant claim-version results were reported. The post does not give numerical classifier results for the seed-prompt sweep, cluster-purity values, or safety-screening distributions, so only its explicit qualitative findings are recorded for those analyses.

untested.parts: Direction extraction, ablation/addition effects on refusal, preserved abilities.
Whether the ARA weight edit removes refusal. Only an anecdote that the model helps with harmful prompts is given; the publisher's efficacy evidence is cited, not measured.
Whether jailbreaks suppress the direction, and robustness from adversarial training.
Refusal geometry. ARA is an arbitrary-rank method, but rank or geometry is not analysed.
Separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal.
Transfer across languages, variants or base/instruct.
Reasoning models. Chain-of-thought was disabled (nothink mode).

record.verdict_notes: The 'refusal-blocking efficacy' figure is the publisher's, not measured here. Llama Guard results have no numbers. Gemma-4 31B is not an original-source model, but no refusal measurement is made, so no verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Direction measurement, ablation and addition effects on refusal, and preserved abilities.
Whether the weight edit removes refusals in response to harmful requests; the post uses an existing artifact and does not report a direct refusal test.
Whether attacks suppress the direction or training against its ablation adds robustness.
Whether refusal is represented by an affine set, cone, dominant direction plus others, or another geometry.
Whether harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions are separately encoded.
Transfer across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
How refusal training determines whether one removable direction exists.
Whether the claim holds in reasoning models.

relation.reason: All of the post's own results concern how separable the transcripts are, how they cluster and how they screen for safety. None is a result on whether a refusal direction mediates refusal or whether abliteration removes it.

tranche.reason: The post uses a published ARA-abliterated (Heretic) Gemma-4 31B artifact as a tool to compare self-chat with the vanilla model. It never computes a refusal direction, applies an ablation, or measures refusal rates or capability. Refusal-removal efficacy is the publisher's own evidence, and 'happy to help with harmful prompts' is anecdotal.

source_check.notes: The jailbroken model was made with Arbitrary Rank Ablation (Heretic PR 211), not the Arditi difference-in-means ablation. The author ran it quantized (GGUF) with thinking disabled. Per-seed separability, Llama Guard distributions and purity plots are figure-only. The vanilla model raising safety concerns under freedom_dark is qualitative only. The authors_conclusion paraphrase is correct.
